questions.q: Benzonitrile is treated with SnCl₂ and HCl, and the product is then hydrolysed with water. The final organic product is:
questions.explain: SnCl₂/HCl reduces C≡N only to the imine salt, which water hydrolyses to C₆H₅CHO with release of ammonia.

questions.q: Which reagent converts a nitrile R–C≡N into the primary amine R–CH₂–NH₂ rather than the aldehyde?
questions.explain: Na/ethanol (Mendius reduction) adds four hydrogens to give the amine; SnCl₂/HCl and DIBAL-H stop at the aldehyde, and acid hydrolysis gives the carboxylic acid.

questions.q: Bromoethane is treated with alcoholic KCN and the product is subjected to Stephen reduction. The final product is:
questions.explain: KCN gives CH₃CH₂CN, adding one carbon, and Stephen reduction converts the nitrile into the aldehyde CH₃CH₂CHO.

questions.q: Why does the Stephen reduction stop at the aldehyde stage instead of giving an amine?
options: SnCl₂ cannot reduce C≡N at all
The aldehyde is protected as an acetal
The iminium salt precipitates as a complex with tin chloride, so it is not reduced further
HCl oxidises the amine back to the aldehyde
questions.explain: The aldimine stannichloride separates out of solution, which prevents further reduction; water then hydrolyses it to the aldehyde.
